What is AI?

Artificial Intelligence is the science of making machines think. Not just calculate — but reason, learn, and create.

At its core, AI is pattern recognition at a scale no human brain can match — trillions of connections, iterating at the speed of light.

From diagnosing cancer to composing symphonies, AI is reshaping every dimension of human experience. And we are just at the beginning.

The Evolution of Intelligence

Scroll to travel through time

1950
◈

The Turing Test

Alan Turing proposes a test for machine intelligence — if a machine can converse indistinguishably from a human, it thinks.

1956
◉

Birth of AI

The Dartmouth Conference coins the term "Artificial Intelligence." A field — and an era — is born.

1997
◈

Deep Blue Wins

IBM's Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov — the first time a machine defeats a reigning world champion.

2012
◉

Deep Learning Explosion

AlexNet wins ImageNet by a massive margin. Deep neural networks rewrite computer vision overnight.

2016
◈

AlphaGo

DeepMind defeats the world champion at Go — a game with more legal moves than atoms in the observable universe.

2020
◉

GPT-3

OpenAI's GPT-3 writes essays, code, and poetry indistinguishable from human output. Language models enter the mainstream.

2022
◈

Generative AI

DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, and ChatGPT reach 100M users in 60 days. Creativity itself is augmented.

2025
◉

Agents Take Over

Autonomous AI agents plan, code, research, and execute multi-step tasks. The line between tool and collaborator blurs.

2030 ?
∞

AGI Horizon

Artificial General Intelligence — a machine that can learn any intellectual task a human can. The question is no longer if, but when.
